chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A rat died in butter, or oil, or honey.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the butter and the honey, the rat and what is around it are taken out, and the oil is used for lighting (by removing the rat).'

key_terms.جُرَذٌ: A rat (specifically the common house rat, often used in fiqh for impurity rulings)
key_terms.زَيْتٌ: Oil (specifically olive oil or similar liquid oil used for lighting)
key_terms.يُسْتَصْبَحُ بِهِ: It is used for morning/lighting (implies purity and usability)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on food contaminated by a dead rat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a nuanced distinction in Shia fiqh between solid and liquid mediums regarding the impurity (najāsah) of a dead rat: butter and honey are considered fully contaminated and require removal of the rat and surrounding material, whereas oil is deemed pure (ṭāhir) and suitable for lighting after the rat is extracted. This ruling reflects the juristic principle that liquids with higher fluidity and lower viscosity do not retain impurity as strongly as semi-solids, a view supported by scholars like al-Ṭūsī and al-Najāshī in their commentaries on the hadith. The practical implication allows for the preservation of valuable resources like olive oil for illumination, distinguishing it from consumable fats and honey.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A rat dies in butter, or oil, or honey’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the butter and the honey, so seize the rat and what is around it (and throw it away), and the oil you can kindle the light with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the mouse that dies in ghee or oil or honey. He (the Imam) said, ‘In the case of ghee and honey the mouse and whatever has come in contact with it can be taken out; but oil can be used only for lighting during the night.’”
